desc:
A mini Sudoku is a 6 × 6 grid in which every row, every column and every one of the six 2 × 3 boxes (2 rows high, 3 columns wide: rows 0-1, 2-3 or 4-5 combined with columns 0-2 or 3-5) must contain each of the digits 1 to 6 exactly once.

You get a partly filled grid: 0 marks an empty cell, 1..6 a given digit. The given digits never repeat inside a row, column or box. Return the number of different ways to fill all empty cells so that the whole grid becomes a valid mini Sudoku (0 if there is none).

To keep the search small, it is guaranteed that the answer is at most 10000. A valid grid that is already full has exactly one completion (itself).
constraints: The given digits contain no repeated digit in any row, column or box
hints: Fill the empty cells one by one. A digit is allowed in a cell if it does not yet occur in that row, that column or that box.
Keep a bitmask of used digits for each of the 6 rows, 6 columns and 6 boxes. The candidates of a cell are the digits missing from all three masks. The box of cell (r, c) is (r // 2) * 2 + c // 3.
To prune harder, always continue with the empty cell that has the fewest candidates. If some cell has no candidate at all, stop that branch immediately.
editorial: This is plain constraint-satisfaction backtracking. Preload the masks with the given digits, then recursively pick an empty cell, try each digit that is free in its row, column and box, recurse, and undo the placement. Every leaf of the recursion is one valid completion, so the answer is the number of leaves.

Choosing the most constrained empty cell first (the one with the fewest candidates) keeps the tree small: forced cells are filled at once and dead ends are detected early. A completely empty 6 × 6 grid has over 28 million completions, which is why the statement bounds the answer; with at most 10,000 completions the search finishes in a blink. The same machinery solves the full 9 × 9 Sudoku.
solution:
def countMiniSudoku(grid):
    rows, cols, boxes = [0] * 6, [0] * 6, [0] * 6
    empty = []
    for r in range(6):
        for c in range(6):
            v = grid[r][c]
            if v:
                bit = 1 << v
                rows[r] |= bit
                cols[c] |= bit
                boxes[(r // 2) * 2 + c // 3] |= bit
            else:
                empty.append((r, c))
    FULL = 0b1111110

    def go(k):
        if k == len(empty):
            return 1
        best, best_mask, best_n = k, 0, 7
        for i in range(k, len(empty)):
            r, c = empty[i]
            m = FULL & ~(rows[r] | cols[c] | boxes[(r // 2) * 2 + c // 3])
            n = bin(m).count("1")
            if n < best_n:
                best, best_mask, best_n = i, m, n
                if n == 0:
                    return 0
        empty[k], empty[best] = empty[best], empty[k]
        r, c = empty[k]
        b = (r // 2) * 2 + c // 3
        total = 0
        m = best_mask
        while m:
            bit = m & -m
            m ^= bit
            rows[r] |= bit
            cols[c] |= bit
            boxes[b] |= bit
            total += go(k + 1)
            rows[r] ^= bit
            cols[c] ^= bit
            boxes[b] ^= bit
        empty[k], empty[best] = empty[best], empty[k]
        return total

    return go(0)
